literature.headline_zh: 猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: MPXV 预先暴露于精液会显着增加原代人成纤维细胞和角质形成细胞的感染。SEVI 增强了上皮细胞、原代单核细胞和离体人体皮肤以及临床 MPXV 分离株和其他 正痘病毒 的感染。SEVI 增加了病毒粒子的附着和摄取,而 CLR01 破坏了精液淀粉样蛋白并消除了增强。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2703396]
参与者描述了对 猴痘 的有限且不断发展的知识,信息主要通过社交媒体、同行网络和新闻媒体获得;猴痘 消息经常被认为是侮辱性的和基于身份的,塑造了易感性的看法并加剧了对歧视的担忧。 [10.1177/10872914261471238]
结构叠加显示人源化变体和亲本单克隆抗体之间具有高度构象保守性(RMSD < 0.6 Å),两种变体都保留了具有天然人性特征的完整表位特异性,并且与 7D11 相比,POX1.1 对痘苗病毒 (VACV) 和 MPXV 的中和作用增强。 [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106405]
该混合模型在 Monkeypox 数据集上实现了 95.17% 的准确度和 95.04% F1 分数,在 COVID-19 数据集上实现了 92.15% 的准确度和 91.87% F1 分数,在 SemEval-2014 上实现了 87.68% 的准确度和 87.12% F1 分数,优于传统和基于 Transformer 的基线。 [10.1016/j.eij.2026.101028]
结果表明,k-GCN 模型捕获了模拟图组织数据中的相关时间和结构依赖性。在模拟情景中,包括有针对性的 疫苗接种、隔离和 储存宿主 定向啮齿动物控制在内的组合策略最大程度地减少了人类感染和流行病负担。 [10.1007/s13721-026-00836-x]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Pre-exposure of MPXV to seminal fluid markedly increased infection of primary human fibroblasts and keratinocytes. SEVI enhanced infection of epithelial cells, primary monocytes, and ex vivo human skin, as well as clinical MPXV isolates and other orthopoxviruses. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2703396]

Participants described limited and evolving knowledge of Mpox, with information obtained primarily through social media, peer networks, and news media; Mpox messaging was frequently perceived as stigmatizing and identity-based, shaping perceptions of susceptibility and contributing to concerns about discrimination. [10.1177/10872914261471238]

Structural superimposition showed high conformational conservation between humanised variants and parental mAbs (RMSD < 0.6 Å), both variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles, and POX1.1 exhibited enhanced neutralisation against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV compared with 7D11. [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106405]

The hybrid model achieved 95.17% accuracy and 95.04% F1-score on the Monkeypox dataset, 92.15% accuracy and 91.87% F1-score on the COVID-19 dataset, and 87.68% accuracy and 87.12% F1-score on SemEval-2014, outperforming traditional and transformer-based baselines. [10.1016/j.eij.2026.101028]
The results indicate that the k-GCN model captures relevant temporal and structural dependencies in the simulated graph-organized data. [10.1007/s13721-026-00836-x]

literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
Pre-exposure of MPXV to seminal fluid markedly increased infection of primary human fibroblasts and keratinocytes.

Participants described limited and evolving knowledge of Mpox, with information obtained primarily through social media, peer networks, and news media; Mpox messaging was frequently perceived as stigmatizing and identity-based, shaping perceptions of susceptibility and contributing to concerns about discrimination.

Structural superimposition showed high conformational conservation between humanised variants and parental mAbs (RMSD < 0.6 Å), both variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles, and POX1.1 exhibited enhanced neutralisation against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV compared with 7D11.

literature.zh: 本期猴痘病毒(Mpox病毒)研究集中呈现以下进展。；MPXV 预先暴露于精液会显着增加原代人成纤维细胞和角质形成细胞的感染。SEVI 增强了上皮细胞、原代单核细胞和离体人体皮肤以及临床 MPXV 分离株和其他 正痘病毒 的感染。SEVI 增加了病毒粒子的附着和摄取,而 CLR01 破坏了精液淀粉样蛋白并消除了增强。；参与者描述了对 猴痘 的有限且不断发展的知识,信息主要通过社交媒体、同行网络和新闻媒体获得;猴痘 消息经常被认为是侮辱性的和基于身份的,塑造了易感性的看法并加剧了对歧视的担忧。 [10.1177/10872914261471238]。；结构叠加显示人源化变体和亲本单克隆抗体之间具有高度构象保守性(RMSD < 0.6 Å),两种变体都保留了具有天然人性特征的完整表位特异性,并且与 7D11 相比,POX1.1 对痘苗病毒 (VACV) 和 MPXV 的中和作用增强。；该混合模型在 Monkeypox 数据集上实现了 95.17% 的准确度和 95.04% F1 分数,在 COVID-19 数据集上实现了 92.15% 的准确度和 91.87% F1 分数,在 SemEval-2014 上实现了 87.68% 的准确度和 87.12% F1 分数,优于传统和基于 Transformer 的基线。
literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. Pre-exposure of MPXV to seminal fluid markedly increased infection of primary human fibroblasts and keratinocytes. Participants described limited and evolving knowledge of Mpox, with information obtained primarily through social media, peer networks, and news media; Mpox messaging was frequently perceived as stigmatizing and identity-based, shaping perceptions of susceptibility and contributing to concerns about discrimination. Structural superimposition showed high conformational conservation between humanised variants and parental mAbs (RMSD < 0.6 Å), both variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles, and POX1.1 exhibited enhanced neutralisation against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV compared with 7D11. The hybrid model achieved 95.17% accuracy and 95.04% F1-score on the Monkeypox dataset, 92.15% accuracy and 91.87% F1-score on the COVID-19 dataset, and 87.68% accuracy and 87.12% F1-score on SemEval-2014, outperforming traditional and transformer-based baselines.

papers.title: From behavioral to structural correlates: a multi-phase analysis of global reported mpox
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Mpox epidemiology has expanded from endemic zoonotic spillover to sustained human-to-human transmission. While behavioral risk factors have been well recognized, how macro-level correlates of mpox burden vary across epidemic phases remains insufficiently quantified, limiting targeted public health responses. Methods Using World Health Organization (WHO) global daily mpox surveillance data from January 1, 2022 to April 30, 2025, we calculated country-period reported mpox incidence and developed a phase-sensitive analytical framework integrating multi-domain macro-level variables across distinct epidemic phases. Five ensemble machine learning models (eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Random Forest, Categorical Boosting) were optimized, and their outputs were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to identify the changing correlates of mpox burden across phases. Results Reported mpox incidence exhibited four temporal-epidemiological phases, comprising localized sporadic emergence, accelerated global spread, sustained dissemination, and region-specific resurgence. SHAP-based interpretation revealed a phase-dependent shift in model-associated correlates, from behavioral factors in earlier phases, such as close-contact networks and population mobility, to later structural vulnerability indicators related to socioeconomic disparities and health-system capacity. The LGBT+ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and other sexual and gender minorities) Legal Index was the strongest overall predictor, accounting for 13.5% of the overall SHAP importance. Its association with reported mpox incidence was context-dependent, with positive contributions occurring in legally inclusive settings and negative contributions observed in restrictive settings, a pattern consistent with differential case ascertainment and reporting visibility. Conclusions Our findings highlight a transition from behavioral to structural indicators in global mpox burden, uncovering phase-specific and geographic heterogeneity. These results support phase-tailored interventions that combine early targeted prevention with later health-system strengthening, equitable surveillance, community support, and stigma reduction.
authors: Y I P E N G Yin

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed global mpox surveillance data from 2022-2025 to identify how correlates of mpox burden change across epidemic phases. The LGBT+ Legal Index emerged as the strongest predictor, with context-dependent associations reflecting differential reporting. These findings support phase-tailored public health interventions combining early targeted prevention with later health-system strengthening and stigma reduction.

papers.title_zh: 从行为相关性到结构性相关性:对全球报告的 猴痘 的多阶段分析
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Mpox epidemiology has expanded from endemic zoonotic spillover to sustained human-to-human transmission. While behavioral risk factors have been well recognized, how macro-level correlates of mpox burden vary across epidemic phases remains insufficiently quantified, limiting targeted public health responses. Methods Using World Health Organization (WHO) global daily mpox surveillance data from January 1, 2022 to April 30, 2025, we calculated country-period reported mpox incidence and developed a phase-sensitive analytical framework integrating multi-domain macro-level variables across distinct epidemic phases. Five ensemble machine learning models (eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Random Forest, Categorical Boosting) were optimized, and their outputs were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values to identify the changing correlates of mpox burden across phases. Results Reported mpox incidence exhibited four temporal-epidemiological phases, comprising localized sporadic emergence, accelerated global spread, sustained dissemination, and region-specific resurgence. SHAP-based interpretation revealed a phase-dependent shift in model-associated correlates, from behavioral factors in earlier phases, such as close-contact networks and population mobility, to later structural vulnerability indicators related to socioeconomic disparities and health-system capacity. The LGBT+ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and other sexual and gender minorities) Legal Index was the strongest overall predictor, accounting for 13.5% of the overall SHAP importance. Its association with reported mpox incidence was context-dependent, with positive contributions occurring in legally inclusive settings and negative contributions observed in restrictive settings, a pattern consistent with differential case ascertainment and reporting visibility. Conclusions Our findings highlight a transition from behavioral to structural indicators in global mpox burden, uncovering phase-specific and geographic heterogeneity. These results support phase-tailored interventions that combine early targeted prevention with later health-system strengthening, equitable surveillance, community support, and stigma reduction.

papers.title: The evolution of tecovirimat resistance in an immunocompromised individual with severe mpox infection.
papers.abstract: Tecovirimat is widely used for severe mpox, but resistance is increasingly reported, particularly in immunocompromised hosts. We describe a case of persistent clade IIb mpox in a 43-year-old man with advanced HIV (CD4 23 cells/μL) and disseminated necrotising disease. Despite prolonged tecovirimat therapy, lesions progressed. Serial viral isolates (n=8) obtained over 45 days underwent phenotypic susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing. Tecovirimat susceptibility declined markedly, with a ∼3 log10 increase in IC50 in late isolates. Sequencing identified distinct resistance-associated VP37 mutations (A290V, A295E), emerging in parallel within heterogeneous viral populations. In vitro passaging confirmed rapid enrichment of resistant phenotypes under drug pressure. Susceptibility to cidofovir and brincidofovir was preserved, and initiation of cidofovir was associated with clinical improvement and cessation of new lesions. This case demonstrates rapid intra-host evolution of multi-lineage tecovirimat resistance in severe mpox, highlighting the need for resistance surveillance and alternative or combination antiviral strategies in immunocompromised patients.

papers.title: Seminal fluid enhances monkeypox virus infection via amyloidogenic fibrils
papers.abstract: Mpox is a re-emerging zoonosis caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), with recent outbreaks driven by sexual transmission. How semen contributes to MPXV infection, however, remains unclear. Here, we show that human seminal fluid potently enhances MPXV infection in susceptible target cells. Pre-exposure of MPXV to seminal fluid from multiple donors markedly increased infection of primary human fibroblasts and keratinocytes. Semen-derived peptide fragments that assemble into cationic amyloid fibrils (SEVI and SEM) enhanced infection of epithelial cells, primary monocytes, and ex vivo human skin, as well as clinical MPXV isolates and other orthopoxviruses . SEVI increased virion attachment and uptake, and fibril-targeting molecular tweezer (CLR01) disrupted seminal amyloids and abrogated enhancement. Notably, tecovirimat and brincidofovir retained activity under SEVI-enhanced conditions. These findings identify seminal amyloids as host factors that amplify MPXV infectivity and broaden cell tropism, suggesting that semen actively promotes sexual transmission of mpox.

papers.source_body_en: Mpox is a re-emerging zoonosis caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), with recent outbreaks driven by sexual transmission. How semen contributes to MPXV infection, however, remains unclear. Here, we show that human seminal fluid potently enhances MPXV infection in susceptible target cells. These findings identify seminal amyloids as host factors that amplify MPXV infectivity and broaden cell tropism, suggesting that semen actively promotes sexual transmission of mpox.

papers.title: Understanding Mpox Knowledge, Communication, and Care Engagement Among Black and Latino Gay and Bisexual Men
papers.abstract: The monkeypox (Mpox) disproportionately impacted gay and bisexual men (GBM), particularly Black and Latino communities, yet limited research has examined how these populations understood and navigated Mpox-related information and care during the outbreak. This qualitative study explored health communication, trust, and structural factors influencing Mpox knowledge and health care engagement among Black and Latino GBM. Between November 2023 and May 2024, we conducted 30 semi-structured interviews with Black and Latino GBM recruited from a clinic-based sample in San Diego, California. Interviews explored participants’ Mpox knowledge, information sources, communication practices, and health care experiences. Data were analyzed using a rapid qualitative analysis approach informed by inductive and deductive coding strategies. Participants described limited and evolving knowledge of Mpox, with information obtained primarily through social media, peer networks, and news media. Mpox messaging was frequently perceived as stigmatizing and identity-based, shaping perceptions of susceptibility and contributing to concerns about discrimination. Peer networks emerged as critical sources of information exchange, normalization, and support related to prevention and care. Participants reported stronger engagement in care and vaccine uptake when interacting with providers perceived as affirming, trustworthy, and knowledgeable about LGBTQ+ health. Limited provider competency in LGBTQ+ care undermined trust and willingness to engage health care systems. Structural inequities, including racism, stigma, and barriers to health care access, further shaped participants’ experiences with Mpox prevention. Findings underscore the importance of culturally responsive public health communication, affirming clinical care, and community-informed strategies that leverage peer networks to support equitable Mpox prevention and health care engagement among Black and Latino GBM.

papers.title_zh: 了解 猴痘 黑人和拉丁裔男同性恋和双性恋男性的知识、沟通和护理参与度
papers.source_body_en: The monkeypox (Mpox) disproportionately impacted gay and bisexual men (GBM), particularly Black and Latino communities, yet limited research has examined how these populations understood and navigated Mpox-related information and care during the outbreak. This qualitative study explored health communication, trust, and structural factors influencing Mpox knowledge and health care engagement among Black and Latino GBM. Between November 2023 and May 2024, we conducted 30 semi-structured interviews with Black and Latino GBM recruited from a clinic-based sample in San Diego, California. Interviews explored participants’ Mpox knowledge, information sources, communication practices, and health care experiences. Data were analyzed using a rapid qualitative analysis approach informed by inductive and deductive coding strategies. Participants described limited and evolving knowledge of Mpox, with information obtained primarily through social media, peer networks, and news media. Mpox messaging was frequently perceived as stigmatizing and identity-based, shaping perceptions of susceptibility and contributing to concerns about discrimination. Peer networks emerged as critical sources of information exchange, normalization, and support related to prevention and care. Participants reported stronger engagement in care and vaccine uptake when interacting with providers perceived as affirming, trustworthy, and knowledgeable about LGBTQ+ health. Limited provider competency in LGBTQ+ care undermined trust and willingness to engage health care systems. Structural inequities, including racism, stigma, and barriers to health care access, further shaped participants’ experiences with Mpox prevention. Findings underscore the importance of culturally responsive public health communication, affirming clinical care, and community-informed strategies that leverage peer networks to support equitable Mpox prevention and health care engagement among Black and Latino GBM.

papers.title: Global Trends in Scientific Production on Mpox: A Bibliometric Review
papers.abstract: Background: /Objectives: To analyze the profile of global scientific production on Mpox, highlighting authors, sources, keywords, and trends across different fields of knowledge. Methods: A bibliometric study conducted between December 2024 and March 2025 using the Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane, and PubMed databases, applying Bradford’s, Lotka’s, and Zipf’s laws, in addition to scientific mapping. Results: A total of 1,146 documents were identified, with a predominance of journal articles (724; 62.9%). According to Bradford’s Law, 22 journals concentrated 381 (33.2%) publications. Lotka’s Law revealed author concentration, with one author responsible for 33 (0.5%) articles. Based on Zipf’s Law, 47 (0.74%) words comprised the most frequent “trivial zone.” Co-authorship and keyword mapping demonstrated an interdisciplinary character involving public health, virology, and epidemiology. Conclusions: There was notable progress in research related to predictive factors, transmission, vaccines, and treatments, as well as a growing use of mathematical models. However, gaps remain regarding specific therapies, long-term impacts, and effective preventive measures, underscoring the need for further investigations to ensure rapid responses to future outbreaks.
authors: Neiva José da Luz Dias Junior
Raisa Oksana Lídia Ellis Freire de Sena Garcia da Silva
Adriana de Sá Pinheiro dos Santos

elements_en.study_design_and_population: A bibliometric study was conducted between December 2024 and March 2025 using the Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane, and PubMed databases, applying Bradford’s, Lotka’s, and Zipf’s laws alongside scientific mapping.
elements_en.methods: The analysis applied Bradford’s, Lotka’s, and Zipf’s laws to assess journal concentration, author productivity, and keyword frequency, respectively, and used co-authorship and keyword mapping to evaluate interdisciplinary research patterns.
elements_en.main_results: A total of 1,146 documents were identified, with 724 (62.9%) being journal articles, 22 journals concentrating 381 (33.2%) publications, and one author responsible for 33 (0.5%) articles. Zipf’s Law showed 47 (0.74%) words comprising the most frequent “trivial zone,” while co-authorship and keyword mapping revealed interdisciplinary involvement in public health, virology, and epidemiology.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating significant progress in mpox research, particularly in predictive factors, transmission, vaccines, and treatments, alongside increased use of mathematical models, while highlighting persistent gaps in specific therapies, long-term impacts, and preventive measures.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the importance of coordinated research efforts and targeted investigations to address gaps in mpox therapies and preventive strategies, informing future surveillance, research priorities, and outbreak response planning.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by its reliance on bibliometric methods and preprint data, which may not capture the full scope of ongoing research or reflect the quality of included studies, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描绘 猴痘 上的全球科学成果,以确定不同知识领域的作者、来源、关键词和趋势,满足快速发展的研究成果中的综合需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 3 月期间,利用 Web of Science、Scopus、Cochrane 和 PubMed 数据库进行了一项文献计量研究,应用布拉德福德定律、洛特卡定律和齐普夫定律以及科学制图。
elements_zh.methods: 该分析应用布拉德福德定律、洛特卡定律和齐普夫定律分别评估期刊集中度、作者生产力和关键词频率,并使用共同作者和关键词映射来评估跨学科研究模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 共识别出 1,146 篇文档,其中 724 篇(62.9%)为期刊文章,22 种期刊集中了 381 篇(33.2%)出版物,一名作者负责 33 篇(0.5%)篇文章。Zipf 定律显示 47 个 (0.74%) 个单词构成了最常见的“琐碎区域”,而共同作者和关键词映射则揭示了公共卫生、病毒学和 流行病学 等领域的跨学科参与。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了 猴痘 研究的重大进展,特别是在预测因素、传播、疫苗 和 治疗 方面,以及数学模型的使用增加,同时强调了特定疗法、长期影响和预防措施方面持续存在的差距。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调了协调研究工作和有针对性的调查的重要性,以解决 猴痘 治疗和预防策略的差距,为未来的 监测、研究重点和 暴发 应对计划提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据因其对文献计量方法和预印本数据的依赖而受到限制,这些方法和预印本数据可能无法涵盖正在进行的研究的全部范围或反映纳入研究的质量,因此需要对研究结果进行谨慎解释。

papers.title_zh: 猴痘 上科学生产的全球趋势:文献计量回顾
papers.source_body_en: Background: /Objectives: To analyze the profile of global scientific production on Mpox, highlighting authors, sources, keywords, and trends across different fields of knowledge. Methods: A bibliometric study conducted between December 2024 and March 2025 using the Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane, and PubMed databases, applying Bradford’s, Lotka’s, and Zipf’s laws, in addition to scientific mapping. Results: A total of 1,146 documents were identified, with a predominance of journal articles (724; 62.9%). According to Bradford’s Law, 22 journals concentrated 381 (33.2%) publications. Lotka’s Law revealed author concentration, with one author responsible for 33 (0.5%) articles. Based on Zipf’s Law, 47 (0.74%) words comprised the most frequent “trivial zone.” Co-authorship and keyword mapping demonstrated an interdisciplinary character involving public health, virology, and epidemiology. Conclusions: There was notable progress in research related to predictive factors, transmission, vaccines, and treatments, as well as a growing use of mathematical models. However, gaps remain regarding specific therapies, long-term impacts, and effective preventive measures, underscoring the need for further investigations to ensure rapid responses to future outbreaks.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:/目标:分析 猴痘 上全球科学成果的概况,突出显示不同知识领域的作者、来源、关键词和趋势。方法:2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 3 月期间使用 Web of Science、Scopus、Cochrane 和 PubMed 数据库进行的文献计量研究,除了科学制图之外,还应用了 Bradford 定律、Lotka 定律和 Zipf 定律。结果:共识别出 1,146 篇文档,其中以期刊文章为主(724 篇;62.9%)。根据布拉德福德定律,22 种期刊集中了 381 篇(33.2%)出版物。Lotka 定律揭示了作者的集中度,一位作者负责 33 篇文章(0.5%)。根据齐普夫定律,47 个(0.74%)单词构成了最频繁的“琐碎区域”。共同作者和关键词映射展示了涉及公共卫生、病毒学和 流行病学 的跨学科特征。结论:与预测因素、传播、疫苗 和 治疗 相关的研究取得了显着进展,并且数学模型的使用也越来越多。然而,在具体疗法、长期影响和有效的预防措施方面仍然存在差距,这凸显出需要进一步调查以确保对未来的 暴发 做出快速反应。

papers.title: MMF inhibits poxvirus infection by disrupting IMPDH2 interaction with USP5 and inducing its Rod-and-Ring assemblies.
papers.abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV), a pathogenic orthopoxvirus, has caused major outbreaks and emerged as a global public health threat. Although antivirals approved for smallpox are used therapeutically against monkeypox, their clinical utility is limited by drug availability and emerging resistance. The conserved strategy by which viruses remodel host nucleotide metabolism to secure biosynthetic precursors for replication and spread has emerged as a pivotal target for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. In this study, leveraging the high genetic and biological similarity between vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV, we employed VACV as a surrogate model to screen 10 FDA-approved inhibitors targeting nucleotide metabolism enzymes, aiming to identify potential novel inhibitors against MPXV. Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), an inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase type II (IMPDH2) inhibitor, displayed potent inhibition effects against both VACV and MPXV. Subsequent downstream time-course studies revealed that MMF targets a post-entry stage of the viral replication cycle. Mechanistic studies suggest that MMF inhibits IMPDH2 activity by suppressing ubiquitin-specific protease 5 (USP5)-mediated deubiquitination of IMPDH2 and inducing rod-and-ring (R&R) assembly, leading to reducing dNTP pools and enhancing antiviral effects. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that MMF is an effective antiviral drug against VACV and MPXV infection and establish a host-directed therapeutic strategy to combat future orthopoxvirus outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) has caused major outbreaks and is a global public health threat, yet antivirals approved for smallpox have limited clinical utility due to drug availability and emerging resistance. The study aimed to identify broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics by targeting host nucleotide metabolism, a conserved strategy used by viruses to secure biosynthetic precursors for replication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used vaccinia virus (VACV) as a surrogate model for MPXV due to their high genetic and biological similarity, screening 10 FDA-approved inhibitors targeting nucleotide metabolism enzymes. The research focused on mechanistic and antiviral effects without specifying sample size, participants, or study dates.
analysis.methods: The study screened FDA-approved inhibitors targeting nucleotide metabolism enzymes and identified mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) as a potent inhibitor of both VACV and MPXV. Mechanistic investigations assessed MMF's effects on IMPDH2 activity, USP5-mediated deubiquitination, and induction of rod-and-ring (R&R) assemblies.
analysis.main_results: MMF displayed potent inhibition effects against both VACV and MPXV. Time-course studies revealed that MMF targets a post-entry stage of the viral replication cycle.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that MMF is an effective antiviral drug against VACV and MPXV infection, establishing a host-directed therapeutic strategy to combat future orthopoxvirus outbreaks. The novelty lies in identifying MMF's mechanism of action involving IMPDH2 inhibition and R&R assembly induction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest MMF could serve as a host-directed antiviral therapeutic for orthopoxvirus infections, including MPXV, addressing gaps in current treatment options and resistance challenges.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that antivirals approved for smallpox have limited clinical utility due to drug availability and resistance, implying potential constraints for MMF's translation. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on a surrogate model (VACV) and lacks direct clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the antiviral potential of mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) against monkeypox virus (MPXV) by leveraging vaccinia virus (VACV) as a surrogate model due to their biological similarity. The research screened 10 FDA-approved inhibitors targeting nucleotide metabolism enzymes and identified MMF as a potent inhibitor of both VACV and MPXV. Mechanistic studies revealed that MMF inhibits IMPDH2 activity by suppressing USP5-mediated deubiquitination and inducing rod-and-ring assemblies, reducing dNTP pools and enhancing antiviral effects. Time-course analyses showed MMF targets a post-entry stage of the viral replication cycle. The authors conclude that MMF represents a host-directed therapeutic strategy against orthopoxvirus infections, addressing limitations of current smallpox antivirals such as drug availability and resistance. However, the evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on a surrogate model and lacks direct clinical validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘病毒(MPXV)引起了严重的 暴发 疾病,对全球公共卫生构成威胁,但由于药物可用性和新出现的耐药性,批准用于天花的 抗病毒药物 的临床应用有限。该研究旨在通过靶向 宿主 核苷酸代谢来确定广谱 抗病毒药物 疗法,宿主 核苷酸代谢是病毒用来确保生物合成前体进行复制的保守策略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用痘苗病毒(VACV)作为 MPXV 的替代模型,因为它们具有高度的遗传和生物学相似性,筛选了 10 种 FDA 批准的针对核苷酸代谢酶的抑制剂。该研究重点关注机械效应和 抗病毒药物 效应,但未指定样本量、参与者或研究日期。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究筛选了 FDA 批准的针对核苷酸代谢酶的抑制剂,并确定吗替麦考酚酯 (MMF) 是 VACV 和 MPXV 的有效抑制剂。机理研究评估了 MMF 对 IMPDH2 活性、USP5 介导的去泛素化以及杆环 (R&R) 组装诱导的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: MMF 对 VACV 和 MPXV 均表现出有效的抑制作用。时程研究表明,MMF 针对病毒复制周期的进入后阶段。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,MMF是一种有效对抗VACV和MPXV感染的抗病毒药物药物,建立了针对宿主的治疗策略,以对抗未来的正痘病毒 暴发。新颖之处在于确定了 MMF 的作用机制,涉及 IMPDH2 抑制和 R&R 组装诱导。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,MMF 可以作为 宿主 定向的 抗病毒药物 治疗剂,用于治疗 正痘病毒 感染(包括 MPXV),解决当前 治疗 选择的差距和耐药性挑战。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认,由于药物可用性和耐药性,批准用于天花的 抗病毒药物 的临床实用性有限,这意味着 MMF 转化的潜在限制。证据强度中等,因为该研究依赖于替代模型(VACV)并且缺乏直接的临床验证。

papers.title_zh: MMF 通过破坏 IMPDH2 与 USP5 的相互作用并诱导其杆环组装来抑制痘病毒感染。
papers.source_body_en: Monkeypox virus (MPXV), a pathogenic orthopoxvirus, has caused major outbreaks and emerged as a global public health threat. Although antivirals approved for smallpox are used therapeutically against monkeypox, their clinical utility is limited by drug availability and emerging resistance. The conserved strategy by which viruses remodel host nucleotide metabolism to secure biosynthetic precursors for replication and spread has emerged as a pivotal target for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. In this study, leveraging the high genetic and biological similarity between vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV, we employed VACV as a surrogate model to screen 10 FDA-approved inhibitors targeting nucleotide metabolism enzymes, aiming to identify potential novel inhibitors against MPXV. Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), an inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase type II (IMPDH2) inhibitor, displayed potent inhibition effects against both VACV and MPXV. Subsequent downstream time-course studies revealed that MMF targets a post-entry stage of the viral replication cycle. Mechanistic studies suggest that MMF inhibits IMPDH2 activity by suppressing ubiquitin-specific protease 5 (USP5)-mediated deubiquitination of IMPDH2 and inducing rod-and-ring (R&R) assembly, leading to reducing dNTP pools and enhancing antiviral effects. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that MMF is an effective antiviral drug against VACV and MPXV infection and establish a host-directed therapeutic strategy to combat future orthopoxvirus outbreaks.

papers.title: An experimentally validated structure-based computational framework for humanisation of anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The re-emergence of orthopoxviruses, most notably mpox virus (MPXV), poses a growing global public health threat. Well-characterised murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies are clinically limited by anti-mouse antibody responses, while traditional sequence-based humanisation often impairs antigen-binding activity. METHODS: We developed an experimentally validated structure-guided computational humanisation framework prioritising 3D architectural congruence over sequence identity, integrating Foldseek-based structural alignment and interface-residue constraints. We applied this framework to humanise two murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies (7D11, A27D7), with comprehensive in vitro and in vivo validation. FINDINGS: Structural superimposition confirmed high conformational conservation between the humanised variants (POX1.1 and POX2.1) and their parental mAbs, with root mean square deviation (RMSD) values below 0.6 Å for all variable domains. Both humanised variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles. POX1.1 showed enhanced neutralisation potency against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV, compared with the parental 7D11. POX2.1 preserved the broad cross-reactive binding and the extracellular enveloped virion neutralising activity of the parental A27D7. In the lethal VACV mouse model, both monotherapies conferred significant prophylactic and therapeutic protection, reducing pulmonary viral loads and improving survival. The dual-targeting combination of POX1.1 and POX2.1 achieved markedly improved in vivo efficacy compared with individual antibodies, delivering 100% survival even when administered 2 days post-challenge. In the MPXV CAST/EiJ mouse model, the combination significantly reduced splenomegaly and MPXV DNA loads in plasma, spleen and lung tissues, effectively suppressing systemic viral dissemination. INTERPRETATION: These findings establish that the structure-centric workflow enables efficient humanisation of well-characterised murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies, providing a validated framework to support the development of countermeasures for orthopoxvirus pandemic. FUNDING: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, the Scientific Research Innovation Capability Support Project for Young Faculty and the National Science and Technology Major Project.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The re-emergence of orthopoxviruses, including mpox virus (MPXV), represents a growing global public health threat, and existing murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies face clinical limitations due to anti-mouse immune responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed and validated a structure-guided computational framework to humanise two murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies (7D11 and A27D7), applying in vitro and in vivo assessments to evaluate the humanised variants POX1.1 and POX2.1.
analysis.methods: A structure-guided computational humanisation framework prioritising 3D architectural congruence was used, integrating Foldseek-based structural alignment and interface-residue constraints to humanise the murine antibodies, followed by comprehensive in vitro and in vivo validation.
analysis.main_results: Structural superimposition showed high conformational conservation between humanised variants and parental mAbs (RMSD < 0.6 Å), both variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles, and POX1.1 exhibited enhanced neutralisation against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV compared with 7D11.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the structure-centric workflow enables efficient humanisation of murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies while preserving antigen-binding activity, providing a validated framework to support orthopoxvirus countermeasure development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This framework supports the development of humanised antibodies as countermeasures against orthopoxvirus infections, including mpox, by addressing limitations of murine antibodies and enhancing neutralisation and protective efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on murine models and in vitro assays, which may not fully capture human immune responses or clinical efficacy, indicating a need for further validation in human studies to confirm translational potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the clinical limitations of murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies by developing a structure-guided computational framework to humanise two murine antibodies (7D11 and A27D7) into POX1.1 and POX2.1. The framework prioritises 3D structural conservation over sequence identity, integrating Foldseek-based alignment and interface constraints. Structural analyses confirmed high conformational fidelity (RMSD < 0.6 Å) between humanised and parental antibodies, while functional assays showed retained epitope specificity and enhanced neutralisation for POX1.1 against vaccinia virus and MPXV. In vivo, both humanised antibodies provided significant prophylactic and therapeutic protection in lethal VACV and MPXV mouse models, reducing viral loads and improving survival. Combination therapy achieved 100% survival even when administered two days post-challenge and suppressed systemic dissemination in MPXV-infected mice. The authors conclude that this validated workflow offers a robust platform for developing humanised orthopoxvirus countermeasures.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The re-emergence of orthopoxviruses, most notably mpox virus (MPXV), poses a growing global public health threat. Well-characterised murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies are clinically limited by anti-mouse antibody responses, while traditional sequence-based humanisation often impairs antigen-binding activity. METHODS: We developed an experimentally validated structure-guided computational humanisation framework prioritising 3D architectural congruence over sequence identity, integrating Foldseek-based structural alignment and interface-residue constraints. We applied this framework to humanise two murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies (7D11, A27D7), with comprehensive in vitro and in vivo validation. FINDINGS: Structural superimposition confirmed high conformational conservation between the humanised variants (POX1.1 and POX2.1) and their parental mAbs, with root mean square deviation (RMSD) values below 0.6 Å for all variable domains. Both humanised variants retained full epitope specificity with natural humanness profiles. POX1.1 showed enhanced neutralisation potency against vaccinia virus (VACV) and MPXV, compared with the parental 7D11. POX2.1 preserved the broad cross-reactive binding and the extracellular enveloped virion neutralising activity of the parental A27D7. In the lethal VACV mouse model, both monotherapies conferred significant prophylactic and therapeutic protection, reducing pulmonary viral loads and improving survival. The dual-targeting combination of POX1.1 and POX2.1 achieved markedly improved in vivo efficacy compared with individual antibodies, delivering 100% survival even when administered 2 days post-challenge. In the MPXV CAST/EiJ mouse model, the combination significantly reduced splenomegaly and MPXV DNA loads in plasma, spleen and lung tissues, effectively suppressing systemic viral dissemination. INTERPRETATION: These findings establish that the structure-centric workflow enables efficient humanisation of well-characterised murine anti-orthopoxvirus antibodies, providing a validated framework to support the development of countermeasures for orthopoxvirus pandemic. FUNDING: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, the Scientific Research Innovation Capability Support Project for Young Faculty and the National Science and Technology Major Project.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:正痘病毒,尤其是 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 的重新出现,对全球公共卫生构成了日益严重的威胁。充分表征的鼠抗 正痘病毒 抗体在临床上受到抗小鼠抗体反应的限制,而传统的基于序列的人源化通常会损害抗原结合活性。方法:我们开发了一个经过实验验证的结构引导计算人性化框架,优先考虑 3D 结构一致性而不是序列同一性,整合基于 Foldseek 的结构比对和界面残基约束。我们应用该框架对两种鼠抗 正痘病毒 抗体(7D11、A27D7)进行人源化,并进行了全面的体外和体内验证。结果:结构叠加证实了人源化变体(POX1.1 和 POX2.1)与其亲本 mAb 之间的高度构象保守性,所有可变域的均方根偏差 (RMSD) 值低于 0.6 Å。两种人源化变体都保留了具有自然人性特征的完整表位特异性。与亲本 7D11 相比,POX1.1 对痘苗病毒 (VACV) 和 MPXV 的中和效力增强。POX2.1 保留了亲本 A27D7 的广泛交叉反应结合和细胞外包膜病毒粒子中和活性。在致死性 VACV 小鼠模型中,两种单一疗法均具有显着的预防和治疗保护作用,减少肺部病毒载量并提高生存率。与单独的抗体相比,POX1.1和POX2.1的双靶向组合实现了显着改善的体内功效,即使在攻击后2天施用,也能实现100%的存活率。在 MPXV CAST/EiJ 小鼠模型中,该组合显着减少了脾脏肿大以及血浆、脾脏和肺组织中的 MPXV DNA 载量,有效抑制了全身病毒传播。解释:这些研究结果表明,以结构为中心的工作流程能够有效地人源化特征良好的鼠抗 正痘病毒 抗体,从而提供了一个经过验证的框架来支持针对 正痘病毒 大流行的对策的开发。基金资助:该工作得到了国家自然科学基金委员会、中国医学科学院医学科学创新基金、青年教师科研创新能力支撑项目和国家科技重大专项的支持。

papers.title: A hybrid RoBERTa–BiLSTM framework for aspect-based sentiment analysis of Monkeypox tweets
papers.abstract: The Monkeypox and COVID-19 outbreaks have brought into focus the significance of social media as a real-time source of public health information, where people share their opinions and concerns regarding different health issues. However, the task of reliable aspect-level sentiment extraction is difficult due to the presence of ambiguous language and class imbalance. This paper presents a hybrid model that uses RoBERTa and stacked BiLSTM layers for aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA). The proposed model utilizes the capability of transformers to represent context and the ability of BiLSTM to learn sequential dependencies for fine-grained sentiment classification. The proposed approach is rigorously tested on the primary Monkeypox X (Twitter) large-scale dataset, a generalization COVID-19 Twitter corpus, and the SemEval-2014 ABSA benchmark using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, five-fold cross-validation, and one-way ANOVA testing. The experimental results show that the proposed approach performs better than traditional machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based baselines, achieving an accuracy of 95.17% and an F1-score of 95.04% on the Monkeypox dataset, 92.15% accuracy and 91.87% F1-score on the COVID-19 dataset, and 87.68% accuracy and 87.12% F1-score on the SemEval-2014 dataset. Statistical analysis proves the significance of the performance improvements across all evaluated domains.

The experimental results show that the proposed approach performs better than traditional machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based baselines, achieving an accuracy of 95.17% and an F1-score of 95.04% on the Monkeypox dataset, 92.15% accuracy and 91.87% F1-score on the COVID-19 dataset, and 87.68% accuracy and 87.12% F1-score on the SemEval-2014 dataset. Statistical analysis proves the significance of the performance improvements across all evaluated domains.

papers.full_text: Abstract Mpox, a zoonotic disease of growing global concern, presents significant public health challenges because of the complexity of its transmission dynamics. The need for innovative tools to model and control outbreaks has become increasingly evident in the context of recent global health crises. This study investigates the dynamics of mpox outbreaks through the application of Graph Convolutional Networks (k-GCN model), focusing on two epidemiologically distinct African contexts: the Republic of the Congo (endemic Clade I, zoonotic transmission) and Nigeria (re-emerging Clade II, human-to-human transmission). We conducted simulations using a compartmental model that integrates graph-based contact networks and epidemiological parameters specific to each country. Five intervention scenarios, ranging from no intervention to combined vaccination, quarantine, and rodent culling, were evaluated. A k-GCN model was then trained to predict node classes for the following year based on simulation data, and explainability techniques (saliency maps and integrated gradients) were used to identify the most influential transmission pathways. The results indicate that the k-GCN model captures relevant temporal and structural dependencies in the simulated graph-organized data. Among the simulated scenarios, combined strategies including targeted vaccination, quarantine, and reservoir-directed rodent control produced the largest reductions in human infections and epidemic burden. Explainability analysis suggested that human-rodent interactions were influential during the early epidemic phase, with a gradual shift toward human-to-human transmission over time. The study supports the potential usefulness of combining contact-based models with explainable graph neural networks for scenario-based epidemic analysis. The proposed approach may help compare intervention strategies and generate evidence for public health decision-making, provided that results are interpreted within the assumptions and calibration limits of the model. papers.title_original: Comparing Mpox epidemic controls through simulations and explainable graph convolution networks: A case study in the Republic of the Congo and Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox, a zoonotic disease of growing global concern, presents significant public health challenges because of the complexity of its transmission dynamics. The need for innovative tools to model and control outbreaks has become increasingly evident in the context of recent global health crises.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study investigates the dynamics of mpox outbreaks through the application of Graph Convolutional Networks (k-GCN model), focusing on two epidemiologically distinct African contexts: the Republic of the Congo (endemic Clade I, zoonotic transmission) and Nigeria (re-emerging Clade II, human-to-human transmission).
analysis.methods: We conducted simulations using a compartmental model that integrates graph-based contact networks and epidemiological parameters specific to each country. A k-GCN model was then trained to predict node classes for the following year based on simulation data, and explainability techniques (saliency maps and integrated gradients) were used to identify the most influential transmission pathways.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate that the k-GCN model captures relevant temporal and structural dependencies in the simulated graph-organized data. Among the simulated scenarios, combined strategies including targeted vaccination, quarantine, and reservoir-directed rodent control produced the largest reductions in human infections and epidemic burden.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study supports the potential usefulness of combining contact-based models with explainable graph neural networks for scenario-based epidemic analysis. Explainability analysis suggested that human-rodent interactions were influential during the early epidemic phase, with a gradual shift toward human-to-human transmission over time.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The proposed approach may help compare intervention strategies and generate evidence for public health decision-making, provided that results are interpreted within the assumptions and calibration limits of the model. This could inform targeted public health interventions for mpox control in different epidemiological settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The analysis was conducted entirely on publicly available, anonymized data retrieved from open-access sources, specifically the World Health Organization dashboard on mpox and data extracted from peer-reviewed literature. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on simulated data and model assumptions, which may limit generalizability to real-world scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates mpox outbreak dynamics using Graph Convolutional Networks (k-GCN) in two African contexts: Republic of the Congo (Clade I, zoonotic transmission) and Nigeria (Clade II, human-to-human transmission). The researchers conducted simulations with a compartmental model integrating graph-based contact networks and country-specific epidemiological parameters. They evaluated five intervention scenarios, from no intervention to combined vaccination, quarantine, and rodent culling. The k-GCN model effectively captured temporal and structural dependencies in the data, with combined strategies showing the greatest reduction in human infections. Explainability analysis revealed that human-rodent interactions were most influential early in the epidemic, shifting to human-to-human transmission over time. The study demonstrates the potential of combining contact-based models with explainable graph neural networks for scenario-based epidemic analysis, providing evidence for public health decision-making, though results must be interpreted within model assumptions and calibration limits.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 是一种日益受到全球关注的人畜共患疾病,由于其 猴痘 动态的复杂性,给公共卫生带来了重大挑战。在最近的全球健康危机的背景下,对建模和控制 暴发 的创新工具的需求变得越来越明显。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究通过应用图卷积网络(k-GCN 模型)研究了 猴痘 暴发 的动态,重点关注两个流行病学不同的非洲背景:刚果共和国(地方性分支 I,人畜共患 传播)和尼日利亚(重新出现的分支 II,人与人之间的 传播)。
elements_zh.methods: 我们使用分区模型进行了模拟,该模型集成了基于图形的联系网络和每个国家特定的流行病学参数。然后训练 k-GCN 模型以根据模拟数据预测下一年的节点类别,并使用可解释性技术(显着性图和集成梯度)来识别最有影响力的 传播 路径。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,k-GCN 模型捕获了模拟图组织数据中的相关时间和结构依赖性。在模拟情景中,包括有针对性的 疫苗接种、隔离和 储存宿主 定向啮齿动物控制在内的组合策略最大程度地减少了人类感染和流行病负担。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究支持将基于接触的模型与可解释的图神经网络相结合进行基于场景的流行病分析的潜在用途。可解释性分析表明,人类与啮齿动物的相互作用在流行早期阶段具有影响力,随着时间的推移,人与啮齿动物之间的相互作用逐渐转向人与人之间的 传播。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 所提出的方法可能有助于比较干预策略并为公共卫生决策生成证据,前提是结果在模型的假设和校准限制内进行解释。这可以为不同流行病学环境下 猴痘 控制的有针对性的公共卫生干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该分析完全基于从开放获取来源检索的公开匿名数据,特别是 猴痘 上的世界卫生组织仪表板以及从同行评审文献中提取的数据。证据强度中等,因为该研究依赖于模拟数据和模型假设,这可能会限制对现实世界场景的普遍适用性。

papers.title: Distinct Inflammatory Immune Signature in Acute Mpox Associated with Proctitis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The immunopathogenesis of clade IIb Monkeypox virus (MPXV) infection and its relationship with clinical severity remains poorly defined. We characterised cytokine responses in acute and convalescent mpox to delineate inflammatory profiles. Methods In a multi-centre cohort, we quantified 45 plasma protein biomarkers in three adult groups; acute mpox (PCR-confirmed clade IIb MPXV infection sampled 30 days post infection) and uninfected controls matched for age, sex, race and HIV status. Biomarkers spanned innate and adaptive immune activation, systemic inflammation and tissue repair. Principal component analysis and unsupervised hierarchical clustering defined immune profiles. Associations with clinical features were explored using logistic regression. Results Sixteen participants with acute mpox (median 6 [4–8] days from symptom-onset; 13% vaccinated) were compared to 16 controls. Three immune clusters were identified. Cluster 1 comprised only unvaccinated acute mpox and exhibited a broad inflammatory signature (IFN-γ, CXCL9/10/11, CCL 7/8, IL-6/10, OSM). Cluster 2 displayed elevated TNFSF12 and FLT3LG, suggestive of tissue-remodelling. Cluster 3 demonstrated lower cytokine expression. Mucosal involvement was associated with the inflammatory cluster 1 (OR 7.85, 95% CI 1.02-102.40; p=0.048). Among 25 convalescent participants (median 405 [225-450] days post infection; 12% vaccinated), clustering did not distinguish cases from controls. However, targeted comparisons demonstrated persistent low-grade immune activation (IL-6, OSM) and tissue-remodelling signatures (TGF-α, VEGF-A). Conclusions Acute clade IIb mpox displays distinct inflammatory profiles, with systemic inflammation concentrated among those with mucosal disease. Convalescence shows partial resolution but persistent tissue-repair activity. These pathways may support risk stratification and targeted therapeutic interventions.

elements_zh.main_results: Sixteen participants with acute mpox (median 6 [4–8] days from symptom-onset; 13% vaccinated) were compared to 16 controls. Three immune clusters were identified, with mucosal involvement associated with the inflammatory cluster 1 (OR 7.85, 95% CI 1.02-102.40; p=0.048).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 急性进化枝 IIb 猴痘 显示出独特的炎症特征,全身炎症集中在粘膜疾病患者中。恢复期显示部分消退,但组织修复活性持续存在。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量较小(16 名急性 猴痘 参与者),由于特定的分支 IIb 焦点,因此普遍性有限。由于观察设计和较小的 队列研究,证据强度中等。

papers.title: A novel mathematical model for monkeypox using variable-order Liouville–Caputo fractional derivatives
papers.abstract: In this article, we study a nonlinear model of monkeypox using variable-order V1-type and V2-type Liouville–Caputo fractional derivatives. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the solution for the proposed model. We derive the numerical solution by using a recent predictor-corrector method. We provide graphical analysis for the proposed numerical simulations of the monkeypox model. The given numerical methodology and the dynamical outputs obtained at different fractional orders add significant novelty to the proposed monkeypox model.
papers.journal: International Journal of Modelling and Simulation

papers.title: Community knowledge, risk perceptions, and determinants of mpox in Ethiopia: An application of the Extended Parallel Process Model
papers.abstract: Introduction: Mpox remains a public health threat in Africa, affecting many countries. Ethiopia declared an mpox outbreak on May 26, 2025. Understanding community knowledge and perception is vital for tailoring mpox behavioural interventions. However, there is limited evidence on community knowledge and perceptions of mpox. The Extended Parallel Process Model provides a comprehensive framework for understanding both perceived threat and perceived efficacy. Therefore, this study assessed community knowledge and perceptions of mpox using the Extended Parallel Process Model in Ethiopia, 2025. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Ethiopia using multi-stage systematic random sampling. Adult household members (>18 years) were interviewed; health worker households were excluded. Data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires on socio-demographics, mpox knowledge, and perceived threat. We used the Extended Parallel Process Model (EPPM) to assess perceived threat and perceived efficacy. Data were analysed with descriptive and inferential statistics (ANOVA, logistic regression) using SPSS v26. Results: The median age was 35 years (IQR: 28–44), and 50.8% (397/782) were male. Only 24.6% (192/782) had good mpox knowledge. Positive perceived threat was 45.1%, and positive efficacy was 79.9% (625/782). Threat-efficacy interaction significantly predicted knowledge (p<0.001, ηp2=0.022); positive threat (AOR=1.73, 95%CI:1.21-2.47), can’t read/write (AOR = 0.163; 95% CI: 0.046-0.579), read and write on formal education (AOR = 0.192; 95% CI: 0.074-0.501), farmers (AOR = 0.199; 95% CI: 0.079-0.501), and housewife (AOR = 0.274; 95% CI: 0.138-0.543). The preferred sources of information were mainstream media at 62.4% (488/782), followed by social media at 23.3% (182/782). Conclusions: The Mpox knowledge among the community was low, implying a need for robust public health interventions. Factors such as educational level, occupation, and perceived threat had a significant association with the mpox knowledge of the community. The perceived threat and perceived efficacy interact to shape mpox knowledge. It is recommended that interventions address knowledge and perception gaps, especially considering interventions that reach all audiences, pairing perceived threat with perceived efficacy, and leveraging mass and social media.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 仍然是非洲的公共卫生威胁,埃塞俄比亚于 2025 年 5 月 26 日宣布了 猴痘。然而,关于社区对 猴痘 的了解和看法的证据有限,这对于定制行为干预措施至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年,埃塞俄比亚进行了一项基于社区的横断面研究,采用多阶段系统随机抽样,采访了除卫生工作者家庭之外的成年家庭成员(> 18 岁)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用采访者管理的有关社会人口统计学、猴痘 知识和感知威胁的问卷收集数据,并通过 SPSS v26 使用描述性和推论性统计(方差分析、逻辑回归)进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有 24.6% (192/782) 具有良好的 猴痘 知识,积极感知威胁为 45.1%,积极功效为 79.9% (625/782)。威胁-功效交互显着预测知识(p<0.001,ηp2=0.022),教育水平和职业等因素显示出显着关联。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将低 猴痘 知识解释为表明需要强有力的公共卫生干预措施,感知威胁和功效相互作用以形成知识,这是扩展并行过程模型在这种情况下的新颖应用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,干预措施应解决知识差距,将感知到的威胁与有效性相结合,并利用大众媒体和社交媒体作为首选信息来源(分别为 62.4% 和 23.3%)。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计限制了因果推断,而仅抽象的证据限制了对潜在偏见的评估;然而,大样本量和系统抽样为研究结果提供了适度的可信度。

analysis_en.methods: Data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires on socio-demographics, mpox knowledge, and perceived threat, with analysis using descriptive and inferential statistics (ANOVA, logistic regression) via SPSS v26.
analysis_en.main_results: Only 24.6% (192/782) had good mpox knowledge, with positive perceived threat at 45.1% and positive efficacy at 79.9% (625/782). Threat-efficacy interaction significantly predicted knowledge (p<0.001, ηp2=0.022), with factors like education level and occupation showing significant associations.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret low mpox knowledge as indicating a need for robust public health interventions, with perceived threat and efficacy interacting to shape knowledge, a novel application of the Extended Parallel Process Model in this context.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings suggest interventions should address knowledge gaps, pair perceived threat with efficacy, and leverage mass and social media, which are preferred information sources (62.4% and 23.3%, respectively).
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the abstract-only evidence restricts assessment of potential biases; however, the large sample size and systematic sampling provide moderate confidence in the findings.

papers.title_zh: 埃塞俄比亚的社区知识、风险认知和 猴痘 的决定因素:扩展并行过程模型的应用
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Mpox remains a public health threat in Africa, affecting many countries. Ethiopia declared an mpox outbreak on May 26, 2025. Understanding community knowledge and perception is vital for tailoring mpox behavioural interventions. However, there is limited evidence on community knowledge and perceptions of mpox. The Extended Parallel Process Model provides a comprehensive framework for understanding both perceived threat and perceived efficacy. Therefore, this study assessed community knowledge and perceptions of mpox using the Extended Parallel Process Model in Ethiopia, 2025. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Ethiopia using multi-stage systematic random sampling. Adult household members (>18 years) were interviewed; health worker households were excluded. Data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires on socio-demographics, mpox knowledge, and perceived threat. We used the Extended Parallel Process Model (EPPM) to assess perceived threat and perceived efficacy. Data were analysed with descriptive and inferential statistics (ANOVA, logistic regression) using SPSS v26. Results: The median age was 35 years (IQR: 28–44), and 50.8% (397/782) were male. Only 24.6% (192/782) had good mpox knowledge. Positive perceived threat was 45.1%, and positive efficacy was 79.9% (625/782). Threat-efficacy interaction significantly predicted knowledge (p<0.001, ηp2=0.022); positive threat (AOR=1.73, 95%CI:1.21-2.47), can’t read/write (AOR = 0.163; 95% CI: 0.046-0.579), read and write on formal education (AOR = 0.192; 95% CI: 0.074-0.501), farmers (AOR = 0.199; 95% CI: 0.079-0.501), and housewife (AOR = 0.274; 95% CI: 0.138-0.543). The preferred sources of information were mainstream media at 62.4% (488/782), followed by social media at 23.3% (182/782). Conclusions: The Mpox knowledge among the community was low, implying a need for robust public health interventions. Factors such as educational level, occupation, and perceived threat had a significant association with the mpox knowledge of the community. The perceived threat and perceived efficacy interact to shape mpox knowledge. It is recommended that interventions address knowledge and perception gaps, especially considering interventions that reach all audiences, pairing perceived threat with perceived efficacy, and leveraging mass and social media.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 仍然是非洲的公共卫生威胁,埃塞俄比亚于 2025 年 5 月 26 日宣布了 猴痘。然而,关于社区对 猴痘 的了解和看法的证据有限,这对于定制行为干预措施至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年,埃塞俄比亚进行了一项基于社区的横断面研究,采用多阶段系统随机抽样,采访了除卫生工作者家庭之外的成年家庭成员(> 18 岁)。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用采访者管理的有关社会人口统计学、猴痘 知识和感知威胁的问卷收集数据,并通过 SPSS v26 使用描述性和推论性统计(方差分析、逻辑回归)进行分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 只有 24.6% (192/782) 具有良好的 猴痘 知识,积极感知威胁为 45.1%,积极功效为 79.9% (625/782)。威胁-功效交互显着预测知识(p<0.001,ηp2=0.022),教育水平和职业等因素显示出显着关联。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将低 猴痘 知识解释为表明需要强有力的公共卫生干预措施,感知威胁和功效相互作用以形成知识,这是扩展并行过程模型在这种情况下的新颖应用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,干预措施应解决知识差距,将感知到的威胁与有效性相结合,并利用大众媒体和社交媒体作为首选信息来源(分别为 62.4% 和 23.3%)。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计限制了因果推断,而仅抽象的证据限制了对潜在偏见的评估;然而,大样本量和系统抽样为研究结果提供了适度的可信度。

papers.title: Immune (dys)function in people living with HIV
papers.abstract: People living with HIV require tailored healthcare strategies, including the management of viral (co)infections. To achieve this, a comprehensive understanding of immune (dys)function in response to pathogens such as HIV itself and Mpox virus is essential. The two publications presented herein investigate the adaptive immune response, with a focus on T cell immunity, in people living with HIV receiving medical care at HIV-specialized practices and at a university outpatient clinic in Munich. The patient cohort consists of individuals either initiating or already undergoing antiretroviral therapy. Those under therapy showed undetectable plasma viral loads and stable CD4 T cell counts – except for isolated cases. We conducted an in-depth characterization of follicular (CXCR5+) CD8 T cells: a subpopulation capable of accessing B cell follicles, which is one major site of the latent HIV reservoir. We found that the frequency of these cells negatively correlates with the level of intact pro-viral HIV DNA and that, particularly in individuals treated during acute infections, follicular CD8 T cells exhibit anti-HIV functionality, which can be further enhanced by PD1 inhibition in-vitro. Due to their characteristics, follicular CD8 T cells may play a central role in future functional cure strategies, especially in individuals initiating antiretroviral therapy early during acute HIV infection. The relevance of robust antiviral immunity in people living with HIV extends beyond HIV itself, as recently underlined during the Mpox outbreak in 2022. Therefore, we investigated cellular and humoral adaptive immune responses after Mpox infection or smallpox vaccination in people living with HIV. We could show that both infection and vaccination elicited Mpox-specific immune responses involving both T cells and antibody responses including in people living with HIV with a stable immune function. Taken together, these studies emphasize the need for tailored preventive, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies that account for the unique immune landscape of this population.

analysis.summary_en: This dissertation investigated immune (dys)function in people living with HIV, focusing on adaptive immune responses to HIV and mpox virus. The study characterized follicular CD8 T cells, which can access B cell follicles and are linked to the latent HIV reservoir. In individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy, these cells showed anti-HIV functionality, particularly when therapy was initiated early during acute infection, and their frequency correlated negatively with intact pro-viral HIV DNA. The authors suggest these cells may be pivotal for future functional cure strategies. The work underscores the importance of tailored healthcare for people living with HIV, especially in managing co-infections like mpox, but the evidence is limited to the abstract and lacks detailed methods and statistical outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: HIV 感染者面临着病毒合并感染(包括 猴痘)的独特风险,因此需要量身定制的医疗保健策略。该研究旨在阐明该人群的免疫(功能障碍)功能,特别是对 HIV 和 猴痘病毒 的反应,为有针对性的干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究调查了在艾滋病毒专业诊所和慕尼黑大学门诊部接受护理的艾滋病毒感染者的适应性 免疫应答。患者 队列研究 包括开始或已经接受抗逆转录病毒治疗的个体。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究表征了滤泡 (CXCR5+) CD8 T 细胞,这是一种能够进入 B 细胞滤泡的亚群,而 B 细胞滤泡是潜伏 HIV 储存宿主 的主要位点。作者评估了这些细胞的抗 HIV 功能,并评估了体外 PD1 抑制的效果。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者提出,滤泡 CD8 T 细胞可能在未来的 HIV 功能性治疗策略中发挥核心作用,特别是在急性感染早期开始抗逆转录病毒治疗时。这代表了对具有潜在治疗意义的特定 T 细胞亚群的新关注。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,需要为艾滋病毒感染者制定量身定制的预防、诊断和治疗策略,以适应其独特的免疫状况,特别是在 猴痘 等合并感染的情况下。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计细节、样本量、统计分析或更广泛的研究结果的普遍性。证据仅限于抽象,缺乏方法论和具体结果的细节,需要谨慎解释。

papers.abstract_zh: 艾滋病毒感染者需要量身定制的医疗保健策略,包括病毒(合并)感染的管理。为了实现这一目标,全面了解针对 HIV 本身和 猴痘病毒 等病原体的免疫(功能障碍)功能至关重要。本文提出的两篇出版物研究了在 HIV 专业诊所和慕尼黑大学门诊接受医疗护理的 HIV 感染者的适应性 免疫应答,重点是 T 细胞免疫。患者 队列研究 由正在开始或已经接受抗逆转录病毒治疗的个体组成。接受治疗的患者表现出无法检测到的血浆病毒载量和稳定的 CD4 T 细胞计数——除了个别病例。我们对滤泡 (CXCR5+) CD8 T 细胞进行了深入表征:这是一种能够进入 B 细胞滤泡的亚群,而滤泡是潜伏 HIV 储存宿主 的一个主要位点。我们发现这些细胞的出现频率与完整的前病毒 HIV DNA 水平呈负相关,并且,特别是在急性感染期间接受治疗的个体中,滤泡 CD8 T 细胞表现出抗 HIV 功能,这种功能可以通过体外抑制 PD1 来进一步增强。由于其特性,滤泡 CD8 T 细胞可能在未来的功能性治疗策略中发挥核心作用,特别是对于在急性 HIV 感染期间早期开始抗逆转录病毒治疗的个体。正如最近在 2022 年 猴痘 暴发 期间所强调的那样,HIV 感染者强大的 抗病毒药物 免疫力的相关性超出了 HIV 本身。因此,我们研究了 HIV 感染者在 猴痘 感染或天花 疫苗接种 后的细胞和体液适应性 免疫应答。我们可以证明,感染和 猴痘 都会引发 猴痘 特异性 免疫应答,涉及 T 细胞和抗体反应,包括在具有稳定免疫功能的 HIV 感染者中。总的来说,这些研究强调需要针对该人群独特的免疫状况制定量身定制的预防、诊断和治疗策略。

papers.title: Drivers of Viral Spillover: A Critical Examination of How Pathogens Spread
papers.abstract: The occurrence of viral zoonotic spillover (the transmission of viruses from animals to humans) has attracted worldwide attention due to mounting concerns regarding viral threats such as avian influenza, Hendra, monkeypox, Nipah and bat coronaviruses. It is evident that these events deviate significantly from natural occurrences, being the conflation of ecological, environmental and social factors that are profoundly altering the boundaries between the animal and human domains. Consequently, in order to comprehend both the contemporary and prospective drivers of zoonotic viral spillover, a coordinated, comprehensive global One Health response is essential. The objective of this review is to analyse prevalent pathways of transmission between animal reservoirs and human populations. This examination involves the analysis of historical cases, including those of SARS and Ebola, as well as recent occurrences, such as the global pandemic of SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19). The objective of this review is to comprehend the fundamental mechanisms of cross-species transmission. The development of effective strategies to mitigate the emergence of zoonotic viruses and prevent future pandemics is contingent on a robust understanding of these mechanisms. This analysis is key to identifying pandemic pathogens and preventing the spread of zoonotic viruses. In conclusion, the review provides a thorough evaluation of current global strategies to prevent the spread of zoonotic viruses, highlighting gaps in our understanding and areas for further research.

papers.abstract_zh: 由于人们对禽流感、亨德拉病毒、猴痘、尼帕病毒和蝙蝠冠状病毒等病毒威胁的日益担忧,人畜共患病毒 跨物种溢出(从动物传染给人类的病毒 传播)的出现引起了全世界的关注。显然,这些事件与自然发生的事件有很大偏差,它们是生态、环境和社会因素的综合体,深刻地改变了动物和人类领域之间的界限。因此,为了了解人畜共患病毒 跨物种溢出 的当代和未来驱动因素,协调一致、全面的全球“同一个健康”应对措施至关重要。本综述的目的是分析动物 储存宿主 和人类之间 传播 的普遍通路。这项检查涉及对历史病例的分析,包括 SARS 和埃博拉病毒的病例,以及最近发生的事件,例如 SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19) 的全球大流行。本综述的目的是了解跨物种 传播 的基本机制。制定有效策略来减少人畜共患病毒的出现并预防未来的流行病取决于对这些机制的深入了解。该分析对于识别大流行病原体和防止人畜共患病毒传播至关重要。总之,该审查对当前防止人畜共患病毒传播的全球战略进行了全面评估,突显了我们理解上的差距和需要进一步研究的领域。

papers.full_text: nature microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-026-02432-1 News & views Viral infection Ebola virus persistence and the hidden cost of immune privilege Amal Fahmi, Isabel Schultz-Pernice & Marco P. Alves Human brain organoids reveal how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system. The idea of immune privilege has reshaped our understanding of how the immune system is regulated across tissues. It is viewed as a state of selective immune tolerance characterized by tissue- and organ-specific immune regulation. Classic examples include the central nervous sys- tem (CNS), eyes and testes, where immune surveillance is present but constrained. These sites maintain a highly regulated immunological milieu through cellular barriers, local immunoregulatory mediators and context-dependent modulation of antigen presentation. While this restrained inflammatory tone is essential to preserve the function and integrity of indispensable tissues, it comes at a cost: the same features that limit immunopathology can also reduce pathogen clearance. As a result, immune-privileged niches may be co-opted by pathogens as long-term reservoirs and enable persistence despite systemic immune surveillance. Understanding how viruses exploit these specialized envi- ronments is therefore critical for defining the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse. Numerous studies have characterized viral replication dynamics, transmission and evolution during acute Ebola virus (EBOV) infection. However, increasing evidence indicates that EBOV can persist during the chronic phase, with ongoing viral replication in survivors sup- porting the concept that persistence represents an active infection Check for updates Immune-privileged CNS • Restrained inflammation • Cellular barriers (for example, BBB and choroid plexus) • Antigen drainage (glymphatics and meningeal lymphatics) • Limited immune surveillance EBOV persistence in the brain Virus exploits immune privilege to establish long-term infection The hidden cost Chronic neuroinflammation Type I IFNs and inflammatory mediators Neuron Astrocyte Microglia Oligodendrocyte Defective viral genomes Viral evolution Persistent reservoirs Neuronal dysfunction and injury Fig. 1 | Immune privilege as a double-edged sword during EBOV persistence in the CNS. The CNS maintains a tightly regulated immune environment that limits inflammation and preserves tissue integrity. In human brain organoids, EBOV infects multiple neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia, via viral spread through budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission. Persistent infection is associated with viral evolution and accumulation of defective viral genomes, mechanisms thought to favour chronic low-level replication. In parallel, activated microglia produce pro- inflammatory mediators and type I interferons (IFNs) that may drive chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury. BBB, blood–brain barrier. nature microbiology News & views within immune-privileged reservoirs1. Among these niches, the CNS has emerged as a particularly clinically relevant site, as studies in non- human primates have demonstrated that replication-competent EBOV can remain in the brain after clearance from the periphery, leading to fatal relapses2. Yet the mechanisms underlying EBOV persistence in the human CNS remain poorly understood, leaving key questions unanswered regarding the neural cell populations that support long- term infection and the associated host responses. In this issue of Nature Microbiology, Widerspick and colleagues3 provide mechanistic insights on how orthoebolaviruses exploit the CNS’s immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence. The authors developed a human brain organoid model that enables long-term analysis of orthoebolavirus infection in the human neural tissue and tested EBOV (species Orthoebolavirus zairense), Sudan virus (species Orthoebolavirus sudanense), Reston virus (species Orthoe- bolavirus restonense), and a related filovirus, Marburg virus (species Orthomarburgvirus marburgense). In these organoids, they show that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days within diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes. This persistence, referring to the continued presence of infectious virus or viral genetic material beyond the acute phase of infection, suggests that EBOV can establish a sustained reservoir within human neural tissue. Mechanistically, the study shows that EBOV persistence relies on both canonical viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission through actin-dependent cellular projections and syncytia formation. Cell-to- cell spread is recognized as a potential mechanism of immune evasion, allowing viruses to disseminate while potentially reducing exposure to soluble immune mediators4. Within highly interconnected neural tissue, this mode of spread may be advantageous, as shown by our recent work demonstrating that monkeypox virus exploits neuronal connectivity to propagate while limiting immune exposure5. Widerspick and colleagues observed that long-term persistence of EBOV was associated with ongoing viral evolution together with the accumulation of defective viral genomes. Defective viral genomes are increasingly recognized as regulators of persistent infection because they can attenuate cytopathic replication while allowing for minimal levels of viral activity. By interfering with replication of full-length viral genomes, defective viral genomes have been proposed to modulate viral replication and host responses, potentially reducing cytopathic effects and contributing to persistence6. Importantly, the study iden- tifies marked cell type-specific differences in the host response to persistent EBOV infection. Whereas infected astrocytes remained comparatively quiescent, microglia mounted robust pro-inflammatory and type I interferon responses, identifying these cells as likely drivers of the chronic neuroinflammation associated with EBOV persistence. This observation reinforces the concept that immune privilege may support long-term viral maintenance while allowing inflammatory responses to emerge once local immune activation is engaged (Fig. 1). Similar patterns have been observed in other neurotropic viral infections. Replication-competent Zika virus, for example, can persist in the brains of surviving mice for more than 1 year within inflamma- tory foci enriched in activated microglia and astrocytes, where viral persistence is associated with chronic inflammation and neuronal injury7. More broadly, persistent viral reservoirs represent one of sev- eral proposed mechanisms contributing to post-acute sequelae of infection, including long COVID, in which sustained immune activation may result from a combination of viral persistence, immune dysregula- tion and other host factors8,9. Whether the mechanisms of CNS persis- tence identified for EBOV are conserved among other Orthoebolavirus species such as Bundibugyo virus — the driving pathogen of the current Ebola disease outbreak — remains unclear. Bundibugyo virus has shown evidence of CNS involvement in animal models, with viral antigen and RNA detected in CNS-associated tissues10,11, and long-term neurological sequelae reported in human survivors12. However, whether Bundibugyo virus establishes CNS persistence through similar cellular tropism and host–virus interactions remains unknown. Comparative studies will be required to determine whether CNS persistence represents a conserved feature across all orthoebolaviruses and to define the viral and host determinants that enable long-term infection within neural tissue. Although brain organoids provide a valuable platform to investi- gate EBOV persistence in human neural tissue, they remain a simplified representation of the CNS and do not fully recapitulate the complex immune, barrier and cellular interactions that shape viral persistence within the intact CNS. Consequently, caution is warranted when extrapo- lating these findings to human disease. This is particularly relevant given that the CNS maintains selective communication with the peripheral immune system through structures such as the glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels, which facilitate antigen clearance and immune cross-talk between the brain and peripheral lymphoid organs. The meninges, choroid plexus and perivascular spaces are also recognized as neuroimmune hubs that coordinate immune surveillance, antigen presentation and leukocyte trafficking13. Addressing these ques- tions will be essential to determine whether EBOV persistence reflects escape from immune surveillance or an active adaptation to the CNS environment. Future organoid models incorporating cellular barriers, vascular components and peripheral immune cells will help determine how these virus–host interactions are shaped by neuroimmune com- munication and how EBOV establishes and maintains CNS reservoirs. They may also clarify whether microglia promote or restrict persistence and whether viral evolution within the CNS contributes to relapse or transmission. Collectively, these next-generation human brain models will provide a framework to investigate the mechanisms governing viral persistence in the CNS in a more physiologically relevant context. papers.title_original: Ebola virus persistence and the hidden cost of immune privilege

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system, addressing the knowledge gap regarding the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse in human neural tissue.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The researchers developed a human brain organoid model to analyze orthoebolavirus infection in human neural tissue, testing Ebola virus, Sudan virus, Reston virus, and Marburg virus over a period of up to 120 days.
analysis.methods: The study used human brain organoids to investigate viral persistence, examining viral spread through budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission, as well as viral evolution and accumulation of defective viral genomes.
analysis.main_results: EBOV persisted for up to 120 days in diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes, with persistence associated with ongoing viral evolution and accumulation of defective viral genomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that EBOV exploits the CNS's immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence through mechanisms like cell-to-cell spread and defective viral genomes, providing novel insights into viral adaptation to neural environments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance and prevention strategies by highlighting the CNS as a potential reservoir for EBOV persistence, which could lead to relapses and chronic neuroinflammation in survivors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on an organoid model, which may not fully replicate human CNS complexity, and the uncertainty regarding conservation of mechanisms across other Orthoebolavirus species.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Ebola virus (EBOV) establishes persistent infection in the central nervous system (CNS) using human brain organoids. The researchers found that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days in diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes. Persistence is associated with viral evolution, accumulation of defective viral genomes, and cell-to-cell transmission, which may help the virus evade immune surveillance. The study highlights the CNS as a potential reservoir for EBOV, leading to chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury. While the findings provide novel insights into viral adaptation to immune-privileged environments, caution is warranted when extrapolating these results to human disease due to model limitations.
